tells: A specific, memorable idea only this piece could have: the map of the world is a clockwork model that builds itself, introducing places and the political machinery of the story
Real material and light: engraved metal astrolabe bands, aged wood and brass gears, a parchment map, with warm, glowing light flaring through the bands
Every frame is a poster: a dramatic macro of the dragon engraving, a low-angle city rising, gear-towers with depth of field, and a top-down map with a plumb line
Credits are set in a carved, classical roman-capital style with a small sigil icon, placed into the scene's space; the title lockup carries custom ligature-like scale play ('GAME of THRONES')
Bookend choreography: it opens and closes on the glowing astrolabe, with a top-down map transition that implies a continuous camera journey
gaps: As the benchmark: the map frame is flatter and less lit than the rest; it could carry the same chiaroscuro
Small credit type is sometimes lost against busy mid-tones (frame 2); it could use slightly more local contrast
The warm sepia palette is tightly held; one controlled cold accent per region could add more variety between places

tells: The logomark breaks apart into hundreds of ribbons of colour, so the brand's letterform becomes a spectrum of the stories inside it. That idea belongs to this brand alone.

The motion is clearly choreographed. The mark rotates and its parts stretch apart, then the camera dives into a red-dominant field of stripes and comes out into a starfield. The ribbons converge in perspective, and the shot closes on the solid mark again, which completes the loop.
The palette is planned: red builds into a whole spectrum (pink, teal, violet, blue) and resolves back to red. The light streaks have real glow and grade.
The typography is the logomark itself, built from ribbons. The type and the image are the same object, so no added type is needed.
gaps: The bookend frames are a lone mark on flat black. Compared with C's dense world-building, the opening and closing frames are sparse.
It has no material texture: everything is light, with no physical surface or craft object. C carves, ages and lights real-feeling materials.
As an ident it is short and has one gesture. It has no narrative progression or layered information to match C's journey across a map with a cast of credits.

tells: It is built from photogrammetry and point-cloud material of real buildings. Some frames deliberately break the scan into datamosh, extruded shards and a kaleidoscope folded into a tiny planet. These are authored choices, not a preset.

Each frame does something different (red-mapped alley, extruded terrain, inverted tiny-planet tower, a text-mapped point cloud of a corridor). That variety points to real choreography and a progression through processes.
Monospace text is mapped onto the point-cloud geometry so it reads as a data skin on the space. It is a conceptual move, even if the type is rough.
Against it: the finish is ragged, the red colour treatment is muddy and some frames are visually illegible. That puts it in the experimental-artist or festival-short range, not polished studio work.
gaps: The colour is undisciplined. The red mapping smears into mud, while A and C commit to a controlled palette. It needs a defined grade that holds across sequences.

The typography is incidental. The mapped monospace text gets no scale hierarchy and no hero moment, while C's type is integrated and confident. The words need to be readable and deliberate when they matter.
The frames lack a single clear focal subject or resolution. It needs a compositional anchor in each shot and an ending or reveal that pays off the glitch journey.

tells: The idea is specific to this piece: a clockwork map of a world, where cities grow mechanically from the terrain while the camera flies between them. It sets up the geography and the politics of the story, and only this show could have it.
Every frame is dense and layered: carved astrolabe bands showing an engraved history, bronze clockwork citadels, bone-white mechanical spires, a parchment map with rivers and tree stipple.
The materials are real (patinated brass, carved wood, parchment). Lighting with motivated sun bursts, depth of field and haze gives tactile depth.
The custom engraved serif credits sit inside the world beside small house sigils. The title lockup is framed by the armillary dragon bands, so the type is fully part of the image.
Choreography is visible: armillary sphere, then a fly-over, a mechanical bloom, a cut down to the map, and a return to the sphere for the title. The structure is a loop, and it pays off.
gaps: The warm sepia palette is very consistent but conservative. A's spectrum shows more chromatic risk.
The credit type sits small and similar across shots. A moment of expressive typographic scale would add range.
The map frame is flatter in light and depth than the 3D clockwork shots. It could carry the same tactile lighting throughout.

tells: A specific world-building idea: the map is a clockwork machine, and cities unfold out of gears, so the opening sequence is both orientation and mythology
Dense, tactile frames: engraved bronze armillary band, carved wood, brass cogs and parchment terrain, all with physically plausible light and ambient occlusion
The credits sit inside the world, each paired with a house sigil, in a carefully chosen incised Trajan-like serif that matches the period
The frames progress clearly from a blinding sun-band to the city-machines, the map and the logo lockup, with a consistent camera language
The palette is limited to warm bronze, olive and parchment, motivated by the subject
Every frame works as a poster; the final lockup reprises the opening band
gaps: The credit type is small and set conventionally; it could integrate more expressively with the mechanisms
The logo lockup leans on a familiar bloom-and-light-rays treatment that is less inventive than the rest
The palette is somewhat expected for fantasy; a more surprising colour accent could sharpen it

tells: A specific concept: the logo's ribbon dissolves into a spectrum of filaments, so the brand mark becomes a light tunnel standing for every story on the platform
Clear choreography: logo, then a fold, the ribbon splitting into strands, a dive into a rainbow tunnel and back to a reassembled mark
Considered colour: the brand red fans out into a deliberate spectrum with soft volumetric glow and fine streak detail
A refined finish on the strand edges and the shading of the ribbon fold
gaps: Three of the five frames are a centred mark on black, so the composition has little variety
The light-streak tunnel recalls a familiar 'hyperspace' trope; the middle section needs a more specific image
There is no texture or material beyond glow; the ribbon could gain a richer physical surface

defects: Blocky square artifacts on the terrain surface (frame 3, bottom centre): looks like a shader or tiling fault or compression macroblocking
The surface edge in shots 2 and 4 is a ragged, jagged noise-displaced boundary that reads as unfinished geometry, not a designed edge
SIGNAL title has soft, muddy edges at 100%. The noise fill breaks up letter legibility (the 'NAL' strokes dissolve into the background lines)
Title fades up through a semi-transparent ghosted state, so it never resolves cleanly
The opening orb shot is mostly black frame with faint, low-contrast lines: dead air, and the subject is tiny
Shot 2 is crushed to near-black, and the dark pillar silhouettes are undefined and murky
The background line field is uniform procedural noise with no hierarchy. The same displacement texture covers everything, so it reads as a default noise preset
Blue and orange zones meet at a hard, straight-ish boundary with no transition craft
gaps: Motion: shots run 4–5.5 s with slow, linear camera drifts and texture crawl. Nothing has weight, anticipation or settle, and there is no choreographed handoff between orb, terrain and title. The cuts are hard swaps, not built transitions.

Sound: the track is filtered noise bursts gated in 2 s blocks, a white-noise riser and one impact followed by decaying clicks. It is generic generated sound design with no tonal or musical layer and no mid-range body. Apart from the 15 s hit, the dynamics are the stock riser-then-hit template.

Finish and concept: the 'signal' idea never becomes a specific image (what is transmitted, to whom). The procedural line noise has no light falloff, depth of field or material response. The title lock-up is soft, poorly legible and lands on a flat orange void without rhyming with the opening orb.
